infra.primary.sqlite.description: SQLite-dialect Primary Database providers — a future non-SQLite dialect (e.g. Postgres) would be a sibling layer under infra/primary, not a member here

sqlite.description: D1 runtime database, D1 deployment resource, and memory database are independent doors built on separate private schema and migration modules.

worker.description: Public — createAuthWorker(config) assembles Better Auth over a consumer-provided Primary Database (Cookie Cache, Google, Admin, Device Login, optional Dash, User Admission Policy, origins and cookies) and serves the pages app the built door embeds

ui.description: Connects the Auth Worker's data to the kui-toolkit auth screens; owns no markup of its own
Four page doors (Home Page, Login Screen, Consent Screen, Device Screen) over one same-origin Better Auth client, the User's Sessions and Grants, and one rule for which screen a visitor may see.

client.description: Public — Direct Session Check: React hooks for session state, sign-in, and sign-out

server.description: Public — Server-Side Verification and Access Token verification, the Current Auth identity they resolve to, the Effect RPC and HTTP API integrations that declare each Sibling's Auth Cannotation, and the MCP Server door that accepts only Token Principals

Two verification doors (session, access token) feed one Current Auth module; access-token and mcp share the auth-worker module for the Auth Worker's issuer, JWKS URL, and Access Token claims, whose interior resolver picks a proof per request; each Effect integration declares its Auth Cannotation in an interior authz file beside its Server Implementation; the mcp door verifies Access Tokens on its own wire terms and speaks Current Auth's Token Principal.

app.description: The pages app: a TanStack Start site rendering the ui pages, built by Vite into dist/app and embedded into the worker door by scripts/bundle-app.mts

cli.description: Public — Effect-only: a First-Party CLI's Device Login, its Session Store, and the Session on every RPC call

auth-toolkit.description: Independently consumed doors — worker, client, server, cli, and the infra providers stand alone; the app composes ui and is embedded into the worker door at build time, never imported by it.
